    StartersSumac flatbreads with beet and herb dipsGrilled sumac flatbreads with a pink beet yoghurt dip and a green herb dipHow to make it4 flatbreads2 tbsp olive oil2 tsp sumac1/2 tsp ground turmeric2 beetroots1 garlic clove300g Greek yoghurt2 tbsp chopped herbs (parsley and mint)200g hummusRoast the beetroot at 200°C until tender, then cool and peel.Blend the beetroot with the garlic and some of the yoghurt for a pink dip. Stir the herbs through more yoghurt for a green dip.Brush the flatbreads with oil, dust with sumac and turmeric and grill until blistered. Serve with the dips and hummus.Kijimi snowy city dumplingsSteamed ginger chicken dumplings in hot chicken stock with spring onionHow to make it400g chicken mince1 tbsp grated ginger3 spring onions, sliced, plus extra to serve2 tbsp soy sauce24 dumpling wrappers1 L hot chicken stock2 tbsp chilli oilMix the chicken with the ginger, spring onion and soy.Fill the wrappers and pleat closed.Steam for 10 minutes.Serve a few in each bowl with hot stock, more spring onion and a drizzle of chilli oil.Babu Frik's tiny mushroom toastsThe tiny droidsmith on KijimiHow to make itAs written, serves 4Bite-sized toasts piled with a buttery mushroom, thyme and garlic pâté, topped with a sliver of cornichon and crispy shallot.Small enough for Babu Frik.Fry 300g chopped mushrooms in 40g butter with 2 garlic cloves and thyme until dark and dry.Blitz with 80g cream cheese, salt and pepper until smooth and chill.Cut a baguette into 20 thin slices, brush with oil and toast at 200°C for 6 minutes.Fry 2 sliced shallots in oil until crisp.Spread the pâté on the toasts and top with sliced cornichons and crispy shallots.MainsKef Bir ocean seafood stewFish, prawns and mussels in a saffron fennel tomato brothHow to make it1 fennel bulb, sliced3 garlic cloves, sliced3 tbsp olive oilsaffron threads, a good pinch400g crushed tomatoes1 cup white wine400g white fish fillets, in chunks300g green prawns500g mussels, cleaned4 slices of bread, for garlic toastSoften the fennel and garlic in the oil. Add the saffron, tomatoes and wine.Simmer to a rich broth.Add the fish, prawns and mussels, cover and cook until the mussels open.Toast the bread, rub with a cut garlic clove and serve alongside.Exegol black pepper rib eyeThe whole fleet arriving over ExegolHow to make itAs written, serves 4Rib eye seared in a smoking pan and basted in garlic butter, sliced over buttery mash with a punchy cracked peppercorn cream sauce.Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk.Season 4 rib eye steaks and sear in a smoking pan for 3 minutes, flip, add 40g butter and 2 garlic cloves and baste for 3 minutes.Rest.Add 2 tsp crushed black peppercorns to the pan, then 150ml beef stock, 1 tsp Dijon and 150ml cream and simmer until thick.Slice the steaks over the mash and pour over the sauce.SweetsTwin suns pavlovaMeringue topped with whipped cream, sliced mango and two pools of passionfruitHow to make it4 egg whites220g caster sugar300ml thickened cream, whipped2 mangoes, sliced4 passionfruitsWhisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until glossy.Shape into a round on a lined tray and bake at 120°C. Cool in the oven.Top with whipped cream, mango and two round pools of passionfruit pulp.DrinksLars homestead blue coconut milkCold milk and coconut milk blended with honey and tinted pale blueHow to make it750ml cold milk250ml coconut milk2 tbsp honey1 tsp blue food colouring1 handful iceBlend the milk, coconut milk, honey and ice until frothy.Add a few drops of blue colouring and blend until evenly pale blue.
